h1: The 5 Best Large-Screen Tablets of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five tablets with 13 to 15.6 inch screens compared on display size, listed storage, stylus support and price range for 2026.
summary: The Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra is the name-brand pick at 14.6 inches. The Callsky-Pro 14 offers stylus support for less, the MESWAO reaches 15.6 inches, and the TECLAST T65 is the lowest-priced pick that still crosses 13 inches.
intro: A tablet screen that counts as large starts around 13 inches, and at that size weight and portability matter as much as pixels. The trap is that the biggest panel is not automatically the best one to carry or hold.

We ranked five tablets with screens from 13 to 15.6 inches, using the sizes, storage and features their listings state, along with the price range each falls in. We did not benchmark performance, and several listings are light on detail, so we flag gaps.

products.name: Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra Ai Wifi Model
products.verdict: The established brand with a 14.6 inch screen and 256GB of storage.
products.description:
The Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra lists a 14.6 inch screen and 256GB of storage, and it is the only pick here in the $500+ range.

It leads because it pairs a very large display with a mainstream brand, where the cheaper picks below come from lesser-known makers. The cost is the price: it is the most expensive tablet here by a wide margin.

Buy it if you want a large screen from a brand with established support. Skip it if budget matters more.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want a large screen from a major brand.
products.skipIf: You are on a tight budget.

products.name: Callsky-Pro 14 inch Large Screen Tablet
products.verdict: A 14 inch tablet with stylus support at a mid price.
products.description:
The Callsky-Pro lists a 14 inch screen, stylus support and 16GB in its specs. It falls in the $200 to $500 range.

The ordering here reflects that it offers nearly the screen size of the Samsung for far less, plus stylus support. The tradeoff is a less established brand.

Best for notes, sketching and split-screen work on a big display. Check what the 16GB figure refers to on the listing.
products.idealFor: Note-takers and sketchers who want a big screen.

products.name: MESWAO 15.6 Inch Tablet
products.verdict: The largest screen here at 15.6 inches, with cellular listed.
products.description:
The MESWAO lists a 15.6 inch screen and cellular connectivity, in the $200 to $500 range.

Its position follows from the fact that the size is the standout and the listing is thin on storage and features. Against the Callsky it is bigger but gives you less to verify.

Choose it for a bedside or kitchen screen where size trumps portability. Check storage and cellular details before buying.

products.name: JJGJ 13 Inch Tablet - Android 16 Tablet with Keyboard - 32GB+256GB+2TB
products.verdict: A 13 inch Android 16 tablet that comes with a keyboard.
products.description:
The JJGJ lists a 13 inch screen, Android 16 and a keyboard in the box, in the $200 to $500 range. The title lists 32GB+256GB+2TB.

This slot reflects that the keyboard bundle is useful but the storage figures are confusing. It is the smallest panel in the $200 to $500 group.

Best for typing-heavy use. Confirm exactly what the storage numbers mean before ordering.

products.name: TECLAST T65 13.4" Android16 4G Tablet
products.verdict: The lowest-priced tablet here that still exceeds 13 inches.
products.description:
The TECLAST T65 lists a 13.4 inch screen, Android 16 and 4G, with 20GB in its specs, priced from $100 to $200.

Last place goes to the cheapest, since the listing offers the thinnest detail. It is also the only pick under $200.

Buy it for a large screen at the lowest cost. Check the 20GB figure and 4G bands on the listing.
products.idealFor: Large-screen use on a tight budget.

whatMatters.detail: Screen size is the diagonal in inches. Above 13 inches, tablets become better at split-screen and drawing but harder to hold. Check the exact diagonal in the title.
Storage is where your apps and files live. Some listings mix storage and memory numbers in the title. Look for a clear storage figure before buying.
A stylus helps with notes and sketches, and a keyboard helps with typing. Only some picks list them. Verify what is in the box.
Established brands usually offer easier service and updates. Lesser-known brands often cost less but give you less to verify. Weigh this against price.
A 15.6 inch tablet is closer to a small laptop. If you move it daily, a 13 inch model is easier. Choose by where it will live.

faq.q: What counts as a large-screen tablet?
faq.a: We used 13 inches or more. The picks here run from 13 to 15.6 inches.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake buyers make?
faq.a: Buying size without checking storage. Some listings give confusing storage numbers.

faq.q: Is the Samsung worth it over the Callsky?
faq.a: If brand support matters, yes. The Callsky costs far less and lists stylus support.

faq.q: Does the JJGJ include a keyboard?
faq.a: Its title says it comes with a keyboard. Confirm what is in the box.

faq.q: How do I read the storage numbers?
faq.a: Look for a plain storage figure in the specs. Some titles stack several numbers.

faq.q: Are large tablets easy to carry?
faq.a: Not always. A 15.6 inch model is closer to a small laptop.

finalTake: The Samsung Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra is the best pick if budget allows. The Callsky-Pro 14 is the sensible value choice with stylus support, and the TECLAST T65 is the cheapest way to a large screen. Always confirm storage and box contents before ordering.
